title: fix(organizations): claimOrgSeedOwnership claims by paged predicate writes until no owner-less row is left
body:
Fixes #23054
Clause-②: no — a runtime fix inside one function: no published accept set and no public signature changes (`OrgScopingEngine` is package-private).

## What changed

`claimOrgSeedOwnership` (`packages/plugins/organizations/src/claim-org-seed-ownership.ts`) read each object's owner-less ids once, at `limit: 10_000`, and updated them one at a time. Nothing read again, and the ADR-0093 D7 once-gate never re-runs the claim, so rows past 10,000 stayed owner-less for good.

It now claims by paged predicate writes, the shape the twin `claimSeedOwnership` took in #14530 and #14719:

- **One predicate write per object:** `update(schema.name, { owner_id: owner }, { where: { organization_id: org, owner_id: null }, multi: true, context: CLAIM_WRITE_CTX })`. Below the engine's per-row hook ceiling, that is the whole claim, and it issues no read.
- **A page when the engine refuses it.** Above `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` (10,000) matched rows the engine refuses the write whole with `ERR_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_LIMIT` and writes nothing (ADR-0058 D6). The claim then reads one page of ids (`CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS` = ceiling / 2 = 5,000, under `{ isSystem: true }`), re-owns that page, and retries the whole remainder until one write carries it.
- **The page write keeps the full predicate** and ANDs `id: { $in: page }` onto it. The twin writes the page by id alone. Here, a row claimed by someone else between the page read and its write keeps its owner, and the write never leaves the organization.
- **`count` is the sum of the affected-row counts** of every write the claim made for the object, never a length the function counted itself.
- **Termination guards, each with a warning:** a page that re-owns 0 rows stops the claim (otherwise it would read the same page forever); so does a refused write whose page read finds nothing, and a result that is not an affected-row count. A 1,000-page belt covers a driver that over-reports. Each object is best-effort: a failure is logged with the count already claimed, that count stays in the result, and later objects are still claimed.
- `CLAIM_WRITE_CTX = { isSystem: true, skipAutomations: true }` (#23008) is unchanged and is on every write.

Changeset: `.changeset/23054-org-seed-claim-paged.md` (patch, `@objectstack/organizations`).

One test-infrastructure line beyond the claim file and its tests: `packages/plugins/organizations/vitest.config.ts` gains one anchored alias, `@objectstack/spec/data` to `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`. The claim and its tests now import `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` and `BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_LIMIT_ERROR_CODE` as values, and `check:test-source-alias` refused the suite reading them from `dist/`. This alias is the gate's prescribed fix (precedent: `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/vitest.config.ts`).

## Measurements against the dispatch's hypotheses

- **H1 holds** on `84c4fffbc`. Line 120 is `{ where: { organization_id: organizationId, owner_id: null }, limit: 10_000, fields: ['id'] }`, and line 134 is the per-row `ql.update(schema.name, { id: row.id, owner_id: ownerUserId }, { context: CLAIM_WRITE_CTX })`.
- **H2 holds: the shape fits.**
  - The two doors it uses, `find` and `update(object, data, options?: any)`, are already named on `OrgScopingEngine`, so `org-scoping-engine.ts` is untouched.
  - On a real `ObjectQL` over `SqliteWasmDriver`, with one code-registered hook on the object, a `multi: true` write over 10,500 rows under `{ isSystem: true, skipAutomations: true }` is refused with `code: ERR_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_LIMIT, limit: 10000`, nothing written. The claim then pages to every row. Pinned in the new real-engine case.
  - The `tenant-audit-census` row for this file is unchanged (`update`, `schema.name`, `undecidable`, `elevated`, 1): the write still names `schema.name` at its call site.
- **H3 holds on the predicate path.**
  - `engine.ts` `buildSession` stamps `skipAutomations` and `skipTriggers` on the batch context. `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks` and `buildPerRowAfterContexts` spread that context into every per-row context, and `triggerHooks` skips `entry.meta` hooks.
  - Measured on the real engine: 0 metadata-hook write dispatches over 12 rows (whole-set write) and over 10,500 rows (paged). 2N code-hook dispatches, one per row and phase, and every one carries `skipAutomations: true` and `skipTriggers: true`.
  - Positive controls on the same engine: the same predicate shape under plain `{ isSystem: true }` fires the metadata hook 2N times (12 rows) and 6 times (3 rows). On the paged run, the page read is seen by the metadata hook as `beforeFind`/`afterFind` with `isSystem: true` and no `skipAutomations`.

## Pin: 10,500 owner-less rows are all owned after one pass

- **Real engine** (`claim-org-seed-ownership-dispatch.pin.test.ts`, new case): `SqliteWasmDriver :memory:`, 10,500 owner-less rows in one organization, plus one owned row and one row of another organization. The result is `[{ object: probe_deal, count: 10500 }]`. The read-back sees 10,502 rows and none of the 10,500 is owner-less. The owned row and the foreign row are untouched. There are exactly 10,500 per-row dispatches of each phase.
- **Unit** (`claim-org-seed-ownership.test.ts`): the same pin over a fake that imports `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` (and refuses any non-`multi` write) and models D6 with the contract's own code. Also: a single predicate write and no read below the ceiling; the page/remainder split (5,000 then 5,500) with the predicate on the page write; a row claimed between page read and write is left alone; a page that re-owns 0 rows stops after 2 writes and warns; a later failure keeps the count already landed, and the next object is still claimed.
- **Cost:** the real-engine 10,500 case takes **1,516 ms** on the fix (verbose run, claim blob `d60e2ef023e0`, the same in both commits). On the old single-pass code it took 7,877 ms and 8,396 ms (the two ablation runs below). The unit 10,500 case takes 47 ms. These are shared-box seconds; the ratio is the portable reading. The dispatch-pin file stays under 10 s.

## Negative-pin ablation (committed first, trap-restored)

Run twice: on `1faee8fa7` (the fix commit) and again on the final head `ddefed998` (after the alias commit). Both runs gave the same reading. The mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit x1, blob `d60e2ef023e0` to `7b1b63404b95`, `grep -c 'claimUnowned(io'` 1 to 0, `grep -c 'limit: 10_000'` 1 to 2). It put the old single-pass block back verbatim: the read at `limit: 10_000` and the per-row `update` by id. The run was wrapped in a `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` that restores with `git checkout HEAD --` an absolute path and compares blob hashes.

No build leg: the subject is imported by relative path (`./claim-org-seed-ownership.js`) from both test files, so vitest reads `src/`, not a `dist/`.

Red, real engine:

```text
 × ... [#23054] 10 500 owner-less rows are all owned after one pass: refused whole under the flag, then paged to every row 8396ms
AssertionError: expected [ { object: 'probe_deal', ...(1) } ] to deeply equal [ { object: 'probe_deal', ...(1) } ]
-     "count": 10500,
+     "count": 10000,
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  8 failed | 5 passed (13)
```

The 7 other reds: the unit fakes refuse a by-id write as not `multi` (the old shape), so every claiming unit case answers `[]`, and the "stops after 2 writes" case saw 10,000 writes. The 12-row real-engine case saw the old per-object read (`beforeFind`/`afterFind`) where the fix issues none.

Restore, proven on disk: `blob after restore d60e2ef023e0 == blob at HEAD d60e2ef023e0`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty. Green re-run from the committed state: `Tests 13 passed (13)`. The second run's restore proof is the same: `trap-restore: blob d60e2ef023e0... == HEAD blob`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Local verification (HEAD `ddefed998`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/organizations test`: `Test Files 13 passed (13) · Tests 160 passed (160)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/organizations typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`, test layer included): green, 0 debt.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived the same 64 commands as the dispatch's list. See the report for the per-command readings and the two that need a prerequisite this checkout lacks.

## Acceptance notes

- **Below the ceiling the claim no longer reads.** A metadata-bound `beforeFind` hook on the object therefore no longer sees the claim, and no longer narrows which rows it selects. The selection is the write's own predicate, composed by the same write-scoping middleware chain as any predicate write. The twin has the same shape. The page read on the paged path is still a plain system read.
- **The unit of failure moved from the row to the write.** A hook or validation rule that refuses a predicate write refuses all of it, so that object (or page) stays owner-less, and the warning names the object and what was already claimed. The twin made the same trade.
- **The unreleased sibling changeset will read stale next to this one.** `.changeset/23008-org-seed-claim-skip-automations.md` says "The read is unchanged. The claim's per-object read is still a plain system read." When both compile into the same release, this PR's changeset states the new behaviour. The 23008 file is not edited here; whoever compiles the release may want to drop that bullet.
- **The read no longer accepts a `{ records }` envelope,** matching the twin, which measured that `ObjectQL.find` resolves a bare array. An engine that answered an envelope would page nothing and get a warning, not a silent pass.
- **Not filed (read-only inference, not reproduced):** the twin's page write is by id alone (`{ id: { $in: ids } }`), so a row given a human owner between its page read and its write would be re-owned to the platform admin. It is in `plugin-security`, epic #15194 territory, which this card does not write.
